models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign, light-air pattern over the Aeolians three days out - useful as a trend only, not a forecast for the trip dates.
briefing.synopsis: The current regime across the islands is very light and largely northerly to northeasterly: model consensus has 2-6 kt at Lipari, Panarea, Stromboli, Filicudi and Salina through 2 Oct, with a recurring diurnal swing to N/NNW in the evenings and a light S/SE land breeze overnight at Portorosa. Seas are effectively flat - 0.1-0.4 ft total wave and swell at every island in the consensus (MFWAM and ECMWF WAM 0.25°, both 30 Sep 00Z). There is genuine spread in places: Portorosa at 12:00 today spans 0.6-7.2 kt across models, and 01 Oct 00Z spans 0.2-8.2 kt, so treat the means as indicative only. ECMWF IFS (30 Sep 00Z) and AIFS (30 Sep 06Z) both carry this pattern forward to the end of the data at 06 Oct 23:00; nothing organised shows up in the payload.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the first scheduled night ashore, 3 Oct at Portorosa, the payload scores Portorosa Marina as sheltered (1.00) with 2.3 kt SE, gusts 6.4 kt and 0.1 ft swell - an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, and the only listed option, so the choice does not matter. Nothing in the current data would push the fleet elsewhere. That figure is a three-day-out forecast and will be re-run nightly before arrival.

passage_notes.note: Currently scored go, best slot 06:00-09:00 with 5.8 kt SSE, gusts 11.5 kt, 0.1 ft sea - a dead run, likely a motor-sail. Afternoon slots fall to 2-4 kt.
Go on current data, 1.7-4.1 kt all day, 0.1 ft sea. The 06:00 slot is head to wind at 2.6 kt NE - motoring; later slots free to NNW close reach.
Go throughout, 1.8-5.0 kt NW to N, 0.1 ft sea. Berth at Marina del Gabbiano is rated only workable (0.923), open from every direction and no anchoring.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (6 Oct, 11 nm, 219°T)
passage_notes.note: Go on all slots, 4.0-4.6 kt NNE/NE, gusts to 10.5 kt, 0.2-0.3 ft sea - a run under 5 kt. Drautto buoy field scores 1.00.

passage_notes.leg: Panarea → Filicudi (7 Oct) and Filicudi → Salina (8 Oct)
passage_notes.note: Beyond the forecast horizon of 06 Oct 23:00. Only a rehearsal run against this week's live weather exists - not a forecast for those dates.

cautions: Departure is 3 Oct and the data only reaches 06 Oct 23:00 - the later legs and every berth from Filicudi onward have no real forecast yet.
Forecast stability at 72-120 h lead shows a mean direction shift of 60° between runs (max wind shift 5.1 kt), so wind direction for the trip dates is essentially unresolved even if speeds stay low.
Large model spread at some hours: Portorosa 01 Oct 00Z ranges 0.2-8.2 kt and Filicudi 01 Oct 12Z ranges 2.2-8.9 kt - do not plan off the mean at those hours.
Isolated gust spikes in otherwise light air - Salina 17.7 kt at 01 Oct 18:00, Filicudi 16.9 kt at 01 Oct 12:00 (ECMWF IFS gusts are interval maxima, so they read high in light wind).
If Stromboli is taken, Marina del Gabbiano is exposed from all directions and anchoring is not permitted - its shelter depends entirely on the calm holding.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS (30 Sep 00Z), AIFS (30 Sep 06Z) and ICON-2i (29 Sep 12Z) agree on a light, flat-sea regime and run-to-run wind shifts are under 1 kt on average, but 60° of mean direction scatter at 72-120 h lead means the trip-date detail is not yet settled.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
